name: M1 Identity Colour
text:
My hair was always my best feature. Then menopause happened, and I stopped recognizing it.

Thinner at the part. Drier. A wiry texture I never had. Under the bathroom light I could see pink scalp where I used to not even be able to find my part.

I did what you do. The biotin. The collagen in my coffee. The shampoo that cost more than my groceries. Then rosemary oil, because every woman my age seemed to be talking about it.

I believed in it. I just couldn't keep doing it.

My hair is finer now, so the oil went everywhere. On my fingers. Down my neck. Through the lengths, so by breakfast it looked flat and greasy and I washed it all out. Some nights I was too hot or too tired to bother. The bottle drifted to the back of the shelf and I told myself I'd start over Sunday. I never started over Sunday.

Turns out I'd been putting it in the wrong place. Fingers and droppers put the oil in your hair. Almost none of it reached my scalp.

Then I found a dispenser with hollow silicone tips. You press them along your part and the oil releases right there, on the skin. Nothing runs. Nothing drips. It stays off the lengths. Clear chamber, 1 to 4ml markings. One hand. Two minutes. Works with the oil you already have.

The first night I thought: oh. This is what it's supposed to feel like.

By the end of the first week I hadn't skipped a night. That had never happened.

The habit was always there. The routine just needed to be easier than the reason to quit.

name: M2 Night Pillowcase
text:
My dermatologist told me it was all in my head. At 11:47pm, scratching in the dark, I knew it wasn't.

What changed came from one question I'd never asked.

I'm 56. It started the year my periods stopped. No flakes. Nothing red. Just a dry, tight scalp that woke up the minute I lay down. I'd get up at midnight and stand at the bathroom sink hoping water would help. It didn't. I scratched so much I worried people thought I had lice.

I tried the tea tree. The medicated shampoo. The apple cider vinegar. Washing more. Washing less.

The one thing I kept coming back to was oiling my scalp at night. Rosemary, jojoba, whatever I had. But I hated doing it. Oil on my fingers, through my fine hair, onto the pillowcase. By morning my hair looked like I hadn't washed it in a week. So I skipped it, night after night.

Then one morning I looked at my pillowcase and asked: where is the oil actually going?

Into my hair. Onto my hands. Into the pillow. Everywhere except my scalp, the one place I meant to put it.

So I went looking for a different way and found a dispenser with hollow silicone tips. It's called Ninu. You press the tips along your part and the oil releases right there, on the skin, not through your hair. Nothing runs. Nothing drips. Clear chamber, 1 to 4ml markings. name: M3 Drawer Nothing Changed
text:
Two years since menopause. A drawer full of things for my hair. Nothing changed.

I'm 61. My hair was thick my whole life. Then it thinned at the part, went wiry and stopped growing past my collar. My doctor shrugged. My hairdresser shrugged.

So I bought my way through it. The gummies. The collagen. The $96 shampoo. Two different rosemary oils, because everyone swore by it. A shower cap. A reminder on my phone at 9pm.

Every one of them made me feel like I was doing something. None of them changed what happened at night.

Oil on my fingers. Down my neck. Into my fine hair, so I looked greasy by breakfast. A towel. A sink to wipe. Half the time I skipped it, and blamed myself.

Then I ran a check. A clean white towel over my shoulders, my usual routine, and I looked at three places.

My part. Barely damp.
My fingers. Slick.
The towel. Soaked.

Two years of buying better bottles, and the oil had been going everywhere except my scalp. Like watering the leaves when you meant the roots.
